/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

1. Background
    There are some cases still can not running in multi provider. These PR fix the cases are as fellow:
    - "should work after restarting kube-proxy"
    - "should work after restarting apiserver"

 2. changes 
     refector the approach of restarting kube-proxy and kube-apiserver. Before the case kill the process and make the kubelet to restart the static pod. This PR change to kill the pod, same with the effect of restaring.

@wojtek-t here are some problems need help :)

I find that the case(should work after restarting apiserver) treat apiserver as process before and use shell command to restart it if provider is AWS. 

The PR is merged in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/11056/files.   (seems a bit long ago 😂 ). 
and more detail line in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fa15799f7409b8644221c2b43a494c74aac0c5ee/test/e2e/network/service.go#L3769

In AWS, kube-apiserver must be restart using `sudo /etc/init.d/kube-apiserver restart` ? Can we all treat apiserver as container(pod)? where or how  can I  confirm them?

In other places we've preformed actions on nodes by using a priv pod + exec + nsenter etc.
That approach ought to let us kill a process w/o relying on it being in a pod? Essentially you drop-in replace executing commands over ssh with using a special pod to execute them. The storage tests are an example.

AFAIK It's valid to run kube-proxy as a binary under e.g. systemd instead of as a pod.
@spiffxp add `SkipUnlessComponentRunsAsPodsAndClientCanDeleteThem` up-front check to check the component run as pod.

review_comments: ok, this assumes that kube-proxy runs in a pod, cool

this is the change that worries me, and we need people from sig-testing to chime in.
With the new approach my understanding is that this test will only work when the apiserver runs inside a pod, and I don't know if this will be compatible with the places it was running
will turn the previous auth for help to confirm it. look below.

These checks are a poor proxy for asking "is kube-proxy running in this very specific manner and are we capable of restarting it?"

I might be in favor of abstracting / being more specific about what we're checking for e.g. `skipUnlessClusterComponentRunsAsPodsAndE2ETestClientIsAuthorizedToDeleteThem(component)` or `skipUnlessClusterProviderSupportsComponentRestart(component)` etc.

But I don't think I'm in favor of dropping the up-front check

From the previous version,  the case alreay treat kube-proxy as pod. 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fa15799f7409b8644221c2b43a494c74aac0c5ee/test/e2e/network/service.go#L712

if kube-proxy running as process, no one will restart it. And case can't run.Here are the same. 

Now if no find component pod in function `getComponentPod`, it wil return  error and the case will end with error.
Of cause,  in the front of case,  checking whether component is deploy as pod will be more nice. I will give it a try :)

init(1) ?
I would think anyone running kube-proxy as a process has it under something like systemd.
